fields.System.Title: INT-5 — Data quality
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Find the data problems that quietly cause inventory problems — before a customer finds them.

Scope

In. Five reports: products with no barcode, locations with no capacity, orphaned
reservations, ledger-vs-balance drift, stale projections.

Out. Fixing what they find. Each report produces a list; a human works it.

Design notes

This is the cheapest feature in the backlog and one of the most valuable. Sixteen points
total. Each report is a day or two of work, and each one finds problems that would otherwise
surface months later as unexplainable stock drift.

Each report maps to a specific defect class:

| Report | Prevents |
|---|---|
| No barcode | Manual entry, wrong-item picks clustered on one product |
| No capacity | Putaway suggesting locations that cannot hold the pallet |
| Orphaned reservations | Stock invisible forever after a missed release path |
| Ledger drift | The system's core promise quietly broken |
| Stale projections | Confident, frozen, wrong numbers |

INT-503 and INT-504 are the ones that matter most. They detect the two defect classes
that are otherwise completely silent: a reservation release path someone forgot, and a code path
that wrote a balance without a movement.

A report nobody reads is not a control. Schedule them, and send the output somewhere a
person will see it. Ledger drift in particular should page someone, not fill a log.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Reports built but never read | [doc 08 §9](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
| Ledger drift found and auto-corrected | [doc 08 §9](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
| Orphan checks missing because there are no cross-module FKs | [doc 02 §4](../../../docs/02-architecture-overview.md) |
